import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# VCₙ dimension of convex sets in ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ⁺¹, ℝⁿ⁺²

In the literature it is known that every convex set in ℝ² has VC dimension at most 3,
and there exists a convex set in ℝ³ with infinite VC dimension (even more strongly,
which shatters an infinite set).

This file states that every convex set in ℝⁿ has finite VCₙ dimension, constructs a convex set in
ℝⁿ⁺² with infinite VCₙ dimension (even more strongly, which n-shatters an infinite set),
and conjectures that every convex set in ℝⁿ⁺¹ has finite VCₙ dimension.
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry Pointwise

namespace VCDimConvex

/-  ### What's known in the literature -/

/-- Every convex set in $\mathbb R^2$ has VC dimension at most 3. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52]
lemma hasAddVCDimAtMost_three_of_convex_r2 {C : Set ℝ²} (hC : Convex ℝ C) : HasAddVCDimAtMost C 3 :=
  sorry

/-- There exists a set in $\mathbb R^3$ shattering an infinite set. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52]
lemma exists_infinite_convex_r3_shatters :
    ∃ A C : Set ℝ³, A.Infinite ∧ Convex ℝ C ∧ Shatters {t +ᵥ C | t : ℝ³} A := sorry

/-  ### What's not in the literature -/

/-- There exists a set of infinite $\mathrm{VC}_n$ dimension in $\mathbb R^{n + 2}$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52]
lemma exists_convex_rn_add_two_vc_n_forall_not_hasAddVCNDimAtMost (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ C : Set (Fin (n + 2) → ℝ), Convex ℝ C ∧ ∀ d, ¬ HasAddVCNDimAtMost C n d := sorry

/-  ### Conjectures -/

/-- Not every convex set in $\mathbb R^3$ has
$\mathrm{VC}_2$ dimension at most 1. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 52,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/vcdim-convex-counterexample/blob/ad7ffff1514843c886633f5408c6456dfb2e2a49/formal-conjectures-v4.27.0/VCDimConvexCounterexample.lean"]
lemma hasAddVCNDimAtMost_two_one_of_convex_r3 :
    ¬ ∀ {C : Set ℝ³} (hC : Convex ℝ C),
      HasAddVCNDimAtMost C 2 1 := sorry

/-- Every convex set in $\mathbb R^3$ has
$\mathrm{VC}_2$ dimension at most 2. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
lemma hasAddVCNDimAtMost_two_two_of_convex_r3 {C : Set ℝ³} (hC : Convex ℝ C) :
    HasAddVCNDimAtMost C 2 2 := sorry

/-- For every $n \ge 1$ there exists some $d$ such that every convex set in $\mathbb R^{n + 1}$ has
$\mathrm{VC}_n$ dimension at most $d$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
lemma exists_hasAddVCNDimAtMost_n_of_convex_rn_add_one (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    ∃ d : ℕ, ∀ C : Set (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ), Convex ℝ C → HasAddVCNDimAtMost C n d := sorry

/-- If $n \ge 2$, every convex set in $\mathbb R^{n + 1}$ has $\mathrm{VC}_n$ dimension at most 1.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
lemma hasAddVCNDimAtMost_n_one_of_convex_rn_add_one {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) {C : Set (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ)}
    (hC : Convex ℝ C) : HasAddVCNDimAtMost C n 1 := sorry

end VCDimConvex

status_issues.source_status: Already disproved at n = 2 by KitaKen1's counterexample cited earlier in this same file. That source constructs a convex polyhedron in three dimensions whose 2-by-2 additive grid realizes all sixteen membership patterns under translation, so its additive VC₂ dimension is not at most 1.

status_issues.suggested_change: Mark this variant research solved/disproved. If retaining a theorem stating the established answer, negate the whole universally quantified claim: ¬ ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → ∀ C : Set (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ), Convex ℝ C → HasAddVCNDimAtMost C n 1. Alternatively retire this refuted variant in favor of the existing n = 2 counterexample. This is a status correction, not evidence of a misformalization of the conjecture as originally posed.

reformulations.difference: Relative to the translates case of Naszódi–Taschuk's Theorem 3, Lean permits arbitrary convex sets, not just compact convex bodies with nonempty interior.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For this universal finite-dimensional bound, the extra generality is harmless. A counterexample using an arbitrary convex C would involve only finitely many translated membership tests. Take the convex hull K of all positively labelled test points; K is compact and contained in C, so it avoids all negatively labelled test points. Thickening K by a sufficiently small closed ball preserves every test and gives a convex body with nonempty interior. Thus a counterexample among arbitrary convex sets yields one among convex bodies. The reverse implication is immediate. This comparison concerns the translates specialization of the paper, not its additional assertion about positive homothets.

reformulations.difference: The quantifier includes n = 0, whereas the background literature introduces VC_n for n ≥ 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: At n = 0, the index type Fin 0 → Fin (d + 1) is a singleton and the sum is zero. Consequently HasAddVCNDimAtMost C 0 d holds exactly when C is empty or universal. The convex singleton {0} in Fin 2 → ℝ therefore supplies the n = 0 witness for every d. I proved both this boundary characterization and the equivalence between the complete lower-bound statement quantified over all natural n and its restriction to n ≥ 1. This settles the boundary convention, independently of the missing source for the general construction.

review.notes:
Checked all seven declarations and the definitions they use. No substantiated mathematical misformalization was found, subject to the source-provenance limitations below. There are no answer(...) declarations. Scratch proofs verify the empty/universal cases, the d = 0 and n = 0 characterizations, injectivity forced by a shattering certificate, and invariance under additive coordinate equivalences. Computed grid cardinalities confirm the 4-point and 9-point interpretations of the two VC₂ bounds.

The cited counterexample's substantive proofs kernel-check without sorryAx; the only adaptation needed for the complete external file was qualifying an obsolete diagnostic #check command. All experiments are under /workspace/review/, and the reviewed file still matches the committed hash.

Infinite VC dimension must not generally be identified with shattering an infinite set. The stronger R³ assertion is explicitly advertised as a strengthening and is supported by an adaptation of the paper's paraboloid construction: encode every subset of a countable sequence by a distinct real section parameter and take the convex hull of the selected points, without closure. Strict convexity of the paraboloid prevents adding unselected points on it. The same idea, with n grid coordinates, a section coordinate and a height coordinate, supports the n+2 construction. These observations do not establish the missing bibliographic provenance.
